Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
${{u}_{1},{u}_{2}},$ 
${{v}_{1},{v}_{2}},$ and 
${{w}_{1},{w}_{2},{w}_{3}},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0.$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0.$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0,\,{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{3}=0,\,{w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{3}=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=10-9-1=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthogonal.

- For the set $V,$ notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=4-4+4=4\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthogonal set.

- For the set $W,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=10-9-1=0 & ✓ \\ {w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=0+3-3=0 & ✓ \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=0-3+3=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $W$ is orthogonal.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ and $W$ only".

Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as {u1,u2}, {v1,v2}, and {w1,w2,w3}, respectively.

The sets U,V, and W are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

  • u1⋅u2=0.

  • v1⋅v2=0.

  • w1⋅w2=0,w1⋅w3=0,w2⋅w3=0.

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

  • For the set U, notice that u1⋅u2=[53−1]⋅[2−31]=10−9−1=0✓ So, the set U is orthogonal.

  • For the set V, notice that v1⋅v2=[122]⋅[4−22]=4−4+4=4≠0× So, V is not an orthogonal set.

  • For the set W, notice that w1⋅w2=[531]⋅[2−3−1]=10−9−1=0✓w1⋅w3=[531]⋅[01−3]=0+3−3=0✓w2⋅w3=[2−3−1]⋅[01−3]=0−3+3=0✓ So, the set W is orthogonal.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "U and W only".

Your Answer:
U, V and W
